claims.text: The as-rolled or non-optimized NiFeCoCr-based baseline has a broad distribution of magnetic exchange energies and processing defects.
Low-percentage Cu substitution combined with optimized annealing reduces the spread of local exchange interactions.
Tailored annealing promotes chemical and structural homogenization in the Cu-modified HEA.
Enhanced structural coherence and reduced defect density narrow the distribution of interatomic exchange interactions.
A narrower distribution of exchange interactions produces a more uniform magnetic microstructure and transition at low applied fields.
The FCC additive promotes local ordering.
Local ordering reduces variations in magnetic anisotropy and defect-induced magnetic inhomogeneity.
Reduced magnetic inhomogeneity produces a sharper, nearly second-order magnetic phase transition.
A more uniform magnetic transition lowers magnetic hysteresis.
Improved microstructural coherence maintains high thermal conductivity and mechanical integrity.
Large magnetic entropy change, effective heat transfer, high heat conductivity, mechanical stability, and low hysteresis losses are important requirements for magnetic-refrigeration materials.
The shape and peak magnitude of the magnetic-entropy-change curve affect magnetocaloric refrigerant performance.
Relative to the baseline, Cu substitution plus annealing will increase magnetic entropy change per field increment at approximately 1 T.
Relative to the baseline, Cu substitution plus annealing will produce a narrower and more pronounced magnetic-entropy-change peak.
A narrower magnetic-entropy-change peak indicates a sharper magnetic phase transition.
Relative to the baseline, Cu substitution plus annealing will reduce magnetization hysteresis.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy will retain mechanical stability and exhibit a faster thermal response.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase FCC or BCC HEAs near the target refrigeration temperature and at applied fields of about 1 T.
Formation of secondary phases or substantial deviation from the low Cu concentration range will invalidate the proposed mechanism.
A 3–5 atomic-percent Cu substitution is the controlled composition range proposed for testing.

contradictions.description: The experiment says both alloy sets are processed under identical conditions, but then specifies optimized annealing only for the Cu-containing set; the baseline is also described as as-rolled or non-optimized. Thus Cu addition and annealing are confounded, and the processing conditions are not actually identical.

The hypothesis predicts several distinct benefits, but the falsification rule is phrased conjunctively and may require all listed benefits to fail simultaneously. Failure of an individual central prediction therefore may not count as falsification under the stated rule.
